Microsoft shipped its largest patch release on record yesterday. The September document lists 1,185 CVEs, counting the third-party fixes it republishes. Two of them matter more than the rest, and neither is rated Critical. CVE-2026-85880 sits in Windows ALPC. CVE-2026-81963 sits in the Windows Update Stack. Both are privilege escalation, both rated Important, both already exploited in the wild. Microsoft says so in its own release data. That pair is the triage lesson. A CVSS score tells you what a flaw could do. The exploited flag tells you what it is doing. Patch those two first, then work the Critical list, and stop letting the word Important talk you into next month. https://msrc.microsoft.com/update-guide/releaseNote/2026-Sep #PatchTuesday #InfoSec #CyberSecurity

ReliaQuest has Qilin and Settra both using CVE-2026-0257, an authentication bypass, to open VPN sessions that look like remote work. Exposure depends on configuration: the authentication override cookie feature plus a particular certificate setup, so not every estate is affected. Fixes have been out since 13 May at the vendor's highest urgency. Panorama and Cloud NGFW are unaffected. ReliaQuest found Cobalt Strike and BloodHound after the connections, so the detection surface sits after a successful login, not at it.
